newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil leaves base TBC rate unchanged for June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil leaves base TBC rate unchanged for June.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank said it has left the basic interest rate, known as TBC, for June unchanged at 1.58 percent.
The Monetary Policy Commitee (COPOM) also decided to set June's Basic Assistance Rate or TBAN at 1.78 percent, the same level as May.
The COPOM's decision to leave rates unchanged for the second consecutive month was in line with market expectations.
Most analysts said the government was likely to continue using high rates to have better control of its external accounts.
The TBC rate is used as reference rate for Central Bank rediscount loans and PROER credit lines to finance mergers and buyouts in the private banking sector.
The TBAN is applied to financial institutions that draw more than their limit from Central Bank credit lines.
The TBC and TBAN rates roughly act as floor and ceiling, respectively, for market interest rates in Brazil. ((--Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511 2485412))
